title: Point sections and constant-sheaf reconstruction
statement: Fix $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$ in the point setting [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Put $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and put $L_R(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply $L_R$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ termwise to complexes. Assume these functors are exact and $\Gamma(s,B)=R$ through the constant-value map. Use their explicit adjunction, sending $h:L_RM\to F$ to $(m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m))$, with inverse $t\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U)$ over each object $U$. For every bounded finite-cohomology complex $c$ over $A_{E,n}$, or bounded finitely generated-cohomology complex $c$ over $\mathcal O_E$, its adjunction unit $c\to\Gamma(s,L_Rc)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $L_Rc$ belongs to $D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. In the integral case $c$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and $L_RP$ is a constructible representative of $L_Rc$. For every $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$ with $c=\Gamma(s,C)$, the actual adjunction counit $L_Rc\to C$ is an isomorphism. These units and counits are natural in $c$ and $C$.
